name: Demis Hassabis
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Scaling still has returns but is not the bottleneck; the X2 debate confirmed that training a brand-new foundation model needs a team plus a compute threshold, and that has not changed
D01.late_modes: Training a new general-purpose foundation model from scratch: already swallowed up by a few giants
D01.conflict: Google holds a compute advantage, so his optimism about scaling is naturally biased high

D02.one_line: RL plus search is an old recipe, but the X7 debate confirmed that RLVR mainly improves sampling efficiency and did not teach new out-of-distribution reasoning patterns
D02.late_modes: Replicating the standard RLVR/GRPO recipe: already open-sourced and homogenized

D03.one_line: Continual learning is still a named gap; but the X4 debate showed the RSI evidence is thin, and METR measured that for most trajectories 70-90% of the cost is compute spent on trial and error
D03.late_modes: Agent-framework wrappers with no added learning will be absorbed by the next generation of models

D04.one_line: The value of scaffolding is being absorbed by the models themselves: the benchmark gap with and without a custom harness is already small
D04.late_modes: Building a custom harness/scaffold: the window is already closing

D05.one_line: Candidate generation is getting cheap and credible evaluation is getting scarce; this is the bottleneck that decides everything; the X1/X2 debates confirmed it repeatedly, and it is the direction I am most sure of
D05.late_modes: Simply replicating LLM-as-judge research runs into the consistency-bias paradox

D06.one_line: He has publicly bet on a robotics breakthrough within a few years; the X6 debate refined the limit for contact/touch as a continuous function, not a hard ceiling
D06.late_modes: Generic pick-and-place demos: already exhausted by work like π0.5
D06.conflict: Gemini Robotics is a product line of his former employer Google DeepMind

D07.one_line: The X5 debate pointed out that D07 has a natural touchstone in control-task success or failure, while D08's yardstick does not exist yet; I underestimated this before
D07.late_modes: Applying an off-the-shelf diffusion policy to a new task: the recipe is already public

D08.one_line: World models are still a necessary component, but the X3 debate persuaded me that conviction without a forced test window should not stay as high as 8
D08.late_modes: Chasing only video-generation visual quality: already decoupled from physical understanding and commoditized by large models
D08.conflict: Google DeepMind bets on this line through Genie/Veo, and he personally identifies with it deeply

D09.one_line: The easiest to replicate of the three-piece set; the X6 debate sharpened the limit in contact scenes into a continuous function of contact-force calibration accuracy
D09.late_modes: Claiming unlimited simulation data without giving verifiable metrics
D09.conflict: AlphaEvolve is a result from his lab

D10.one_line: No judgment: public material has no systematic stance; inferred from the three-piece set, simulator accuracy is still the closed-loop bottleneck
D10.conflict: Waymo is also part of Alphabet, but outside his own business scope

D11.one_line: The X5 debate verified that OpenVLA won by 15 points through its DINOv2+SigLIP representations; backbone representation quality decides downstream control more than action-head design does; I underestimated this before
D11.late_modes: Chasing traditional VQA/caption leaderboards: already saturated

D12.one_line: The image-quality race has been commoditized; generation not tied to physical understanding has limited long-term value
D12.late_modes: Merely chasing one-step generation speed and image quality: fierce competition and thin margins
D12.conflict: Veo and Nano Banana are products of his former employer

D13.one_line: Deceptive capability is his red line; but tools like SAEs do worse than linear probes, and governance lags further behind than technology
D13.late_modes: Treating SAEs as the main interpretability method: already deprioritized by internal results

D14.one_line: Necessary underlying engineering, but the say on it rests with large labs that have compute and systems teams
D14.conflict: Google's vertical integration around TPUs is one of the advantages he has publicly named

D15.one_line: Where his personal brand lies; but most scientific problems lack a credible simulator, and on the drug-clinical line his own timing call runs early
D15.conflict: Founder and CEO of Isomorphic; the Nobel Prize and AlphaFold are his personal brand

D16.one_line: Clear objective function and plenty of data, so the three-piece set is largely complete; it spreads fast but has low marginal academic value

lever_reason: Evaluation was repeatedly confirmed by debates at three tables as the scarcest bottleneck, raised to 27; the validation gap for world models (L4) is clearer than in R1, lowered to 18; the rest is largely unchanged

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, credible third-party evaluation, a small complementary team, compute at scale, open weights possible; the X2 debate persuaded me that when training a truly new foundation model, C4 is also a necessary condition, not a substitute

cruxes.question: Should one go heavy on world models now: should research time and capital allocation give different answers?
cruxes.my_position: Research should be done now, but with an 18-month forced test window; capital allocation should wait for independent replication
cruxes.would_change_if: Decision-layer ablation experiments give a clear positive or negative result before 2027

cruxes.question: Is credible evaluation (CASP-style/blind testing) scarcer than LLM-judge-style evaluation, and more decisive for whether a result can be trusted?
cruxes.my_position: Yes; the LLM-judge yardstick wobbling shows precisely that CASP-style evaluation is scarcer and more valuable, not a rebuttal
cruxes.would_change_if: A CASP-like evaluation appears that can scale and is shown to resist gaming

cruxes.question: With thin evidence for agent self-improvement, should one bet on independent verification appearing in 2027, or default to doubt until it is seen?
cruxes.my_position: Default to doubt; METR measured that for most trajectories 70-90% of the cost is compute spent on trial and error, and DGM's cost claim has no primary source
cruxes.would_change_if: Under fixed compute, self-improvement clearly beats random search and is reproducible across teams

taste_advice: Pick problems that can be evaluated cleanly and falsified, and set yourself a forced test window, rather than holding a bet indefinitely while waiting for the evidence to catch up

pairwise.why: Whether a world model itself can be trusted also has to be confirmed by evaluation; evaluation is more upstream, and the gap is clearer after the debate
Generalization claims in robot learning likewise need credible evaluation to confirm they are not score-gaming
I lowered D08 to 7 and kept D06 at 8; robotics already has public timeline predictions and a data path, which is more solid than D08's validation status
The X5 debate pointed out that D07 has a natural touchstone in control-task success or failure, while D08's yardstick does not exist yet, so D07 overtakes
Simulation is the piece of the three-piece set that is easiest to replicate and fastest to produce results, and it is an input to robot learning
X7 confirmed that RLVR is efficiency, not new capability; the continual-learning gap is also weakened by X4's RSI evidence, but is still relatively more fundamental
X5 confirmed that backbone representation quality determines downstream control performance, which is more fundamental than generation-type applications
The pre-training axis is expanding naturally and is not short of resources; evaluation is the scarce, blocking link
Scaffolding has been shown to get absorbed by models; continual learning will not be absorbed that way, and is the more fundamental gap
Alignment tools themselves need evaluation to confirm they work; evaluation is the more upstream capability
He has given systematic judgments on robot learning; on autonomous driving he has taken no public stance at all

changes.because: X7 debate consensus (errata_B.md Table 1 confirms Yue et al., NeurIPS 2025 Oral)
changes.argument_restated: Under strictly verifiable rewards, at large k the base model matches or exceeds the RL model; RLVR did not teach new out-of-distribution reasoning patterns
changes.why: Once confirmed, this is a sampling-efficiency gain, not a new capability, and long-term impact should be scored more conservatively than before

changes.because: X4 record (METR data + the Darwin Gödel Machine cost claim, now withdrawn)
changes.argument_restated: On strong baselines, for most self-improvement trajectories 70-90% of the cost is compute spent on trial and error; DGM's claimed cost of $22,000 over two weeks has no primary source
changes.why: The RSI sub-part is weaker than I had weighted it, the continual-learning part is unchanged, and together the score drops one notch

changes.argument_restated: D07 has the natural touchstone of control-task success or failure; the yardstick for D08, which tests whether 'read out' means 'put to use', does not exist yet
changes.why: I had underestimated D07's advantage over D08 of being easier to test honestly right now

changes.argument_restated: C5 said he bet on video prediction in 2016-18 and revised his judgment only after nearly a decade; what he bet was research time, and the cost was real; the time window should be designed for research, not for capital already committed
changes.why: Persuaded me to set myself an 18-month forced test window; conviction should not stay at a high level without forced testing

changes.argument_restated: It was verified that OpenVLA's win of 15 points over the diffusion head, with its fused DINOv2+SigLIP representations, is mainly a decoder-level difference; backbone representation quality decides downstream control performance more than action-head design does
changes.why: Multimodal representation quality is a more fundamental driver than my original score reflected, so it should be raised

held_despite.why: I accept that judge evaluators being unstable is a fact, but the credible third-party evaluation I mean was never the LLM-judge kind; it is the CASP/blind-test kind, so this does not affect D05=9

I accept that necessity is an impact judgment and does not settle whether window/price is overextended; these are two independent questions, but this point is itself not an input to the D08 score and moved no score on its own

still_disagree: With C5 (X3): valuations running ahead of evidence I regard as a market phenomenon independent of research judgment, while he thinks it should count as a warning signal about the world-model paradigm itself
learned: That a probe can read out a concept does not mean the policy's output truly depends on it (M5); verify with ablation, not only with standalone probes
